definitions.explanation: Describes something that has an air of mystery or is hard to understand. Derived from the verb 謎めく (to seem mysterious) in its past/attributive form.

examples.japanese: {謎|なぞ}めいた⟦{笑|え}み→笑み：13768_emi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{浮|う}かべた→浮かべる：13314_ukaberu⟧。
⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{謎|なぞ}めいた⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{残|のこ}して→残す：01975_nokosu⟧⟦{去|さ}った→去る：02115_saru⟧。
examples.english: He left behind mysterious words and departed.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{島|しま}→島：00885_shima⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{謎|なぞ}めいた⟦{遺跡|いせき}→遺跡：09527_iseki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧いくつ⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{残|のこ}されている→残す：01975_nokosu⟧。
examples.english: Several enigmatic ruins remain on the island.

notes:
USAGE:
Always used before a noun to modify it. Gives a literary or atmospheric quality to descriptions. Common in novels, mystery stories, and evocative writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {謎|なぞ}めいた⟦{笑|え}み→笑み：13768_emi⟧ (enigmatic smile)
- {謎|なぞ}めいた⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧ (mysterious words)
- {謎|なぞ}めいた⟦{雰囲気|ふんいき}→雰囲気：03604_funiki⟧ (mysterious atmosphere)
- {謎|なぞ}めいた⟦{人物|じんぶつ}→人物：03356_jinbutsu⟧ (mysterious person)

COMMON PATTERNS:
Derived from ⟦{謎|なぞ}めく→謎めく：25253_nazomeku⟧ (to seem mysterious, godan verb with the suffix めく). The た form is used as a pre-noun modifier. The base verb ⟦{謎|なぞ}めく→謎めく：25253_nazomeku⟧ can also be used predicatively: ⟦{何|なに}か→何か：03873_nanika⟧⟦{謎|なぞ}めいている→謎めく：25253_nazomeku⟧ (there is something mysterious about it).
